title: The Brars Are Routed and Binjhu Is Emptied

blocks.text: After enduring repeated nuisance and attack, the Singhs resolve to end the trouble decisively and meet the Brars in open fighting. Dust, smoke, and confusion fill the field, but the balance steadily tilts toward the Sikh side as mounted Brars are shot down or driven away.

The scale of the reversal is marked by the capture of fifteen hundred horses, a detail that shows how thoroughly the Brar strength collapses once the battle turns. What began as harassment now ends in rout, with the Singhs seizing animals, prisoners, and the initiative.

A follow-up strike leaves the village Binjhu of the Brars largely emptied as survivors flee toward places like Kotkapoora and Faridkot. The page presents this not as random plunder but as the clearing of a hostile base that had chosen war with the Khalsa.
